core_obligations: Reduce to an infinite base field: base change the linear map along a field extension, noting that the base change of the map for F is the map for the base-changed sheaf, and use faithful flatness (proof lines 6701-6707).
Dispose of n = 0, where O(1) is generated by T_0 (proof lines 6710-6712).
For n > 0 apply the induction-step lemma and tensor by O(m+1) to obtain the short exact sequence 0 -> F(m) -> F(m+1) -> i_*G(m+1) -> 0, and take a section t of F(m+1) (proof lines 6713-6720).

Lift the restriction of t to the hyperplane using the induction hypothesis, and lift t itself using the vanishing H^1(F(m-1)) = 0 implied by m-regularity together with the long exact cohomology sequence (proof lines 6721-6739).
proof_roadmap: Enlarge the base field so that the induction step applies.
Induct on n, with the trivial case n = 0.
Lift the hyperplane restriction and then the section itself using an H^1 vanishing.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves surjectivity of the multiplication map H^0(F(m)) tensor H^0(O(1)) -> H^0(F(m+1)) for an m-regular coherent sheaf on projective n-space. The proof first reduces to an infinite base field: base changing the linear map along a faithfully flat extension of fields preserves it, so the statement may be checked after enlarging k (proof lines 6701-6707). It then inducts on n: the case n = 0 is trivial, and for n > 0 it applies the induction-step sequence tensored by O(m+1), takes a section t of the (m+1)-st twist, uses the induction hypothesis to lift its restriction to the hyperplane, and uses the vanishing H^1(F(m-1)) = 0 supplied by m-regularity together with the long exact sequence to lift t itself (proof lines 6710-6739). H2: the field reduction and the two-stage lifting through the exact sequence are the substance.
